rv.q: Even with your eyes closed, it’s every bit as enchanting.
There's something joyful about watching the cast throw everything at this production.

It's a lean and resourceful production. Close your eyes and it's just as enjoyable to listen to – especially during busy scenes where those not actively involved are huddled around a separate mic, creating whispered chatter.
It is such a cheering, effective production that everybody should see it, especially at this moment in time when so much of the world is in despair at the cruelty of the Mr Potters in power.
Watching six talented performers conjure an entire town out of thin air using only vintage microphones and theatrical ingenuity makes for an engaging evening.
This production of It's a Wonderful Life! is wonderful in its entirety.
In an impressively innovative production at Jermyn Street Theatre directed by Jessica Lazar and boosted by a versatile, multi-roling cast, the show is a genuine Christmas treat.

So here I was, Friday night in the wonderful Jermyn Street Theatre, packed with wonderfully happy people, seeing a play I wasn’t too keen on. I could see that Griffin Stevens, a James Stewart lookalike, had been cast as George Bailey, and who pulled off a good impression of that wonderful actor.
It is a Christmas treat not to be missed.
This bijou miracle of compression is worth snatching the last ticket for, like (let's be schmaltzy) a stray petal from Zuzu's flower. Outstanding, of course.
